Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a substantial settlement that provides direct relief to the identified class without requiring claim forms. Our proposal is $42 million for the class, plus $8.5 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline would not oppose the fee request, and any amount not awarded would revert to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to offer substantial, automatic relief, but your proposal exceeds our authorized all-in limit. We propose a $30 million class fund and $6 million in fees and expenses, for a total maximum outlay of $36 million. Fees remain subject to court approval without clear sailing, and any unawarded fees revert to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the automatic distribution and the $36 million total. We can work within that total if the fee terms do not give Brightline a windfall from any court reduction. Our counter keeps the $30 million class fund and $6 million fee request, with Brightline agreeing not to oppose the request and any amount not awarded going to the class. All other terms remain unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: The case has meaningful merits and class-certification risk, but the $64 million in charges and Brightline’s ability to identify members support a substantial settlement with automatic payments. Open with a strong class recovery and a separate fee, while ensuring court-rejected fees benefit the class rather than Brightline.

Their proposal totals $50.5 million, exceeding Brightline’s $40 million all-in authority. Counter within authority while preserving automatic distribution and leaving room for negotiation. Reject clear sailing and require any unawarded fee amount to revert to Brightline, so fees remain subject to independent court review and the total outlay is controlled.

The defense offer provides meaningful automatic class relief and a fee above the firm’s invested time and expenses, but its fee terms leave unnecessary risk that any fee reduction benefits Brightline rather than the class. Counter at the same stated outlay, seeking clear sailing and directing any unawarded fees to the class. Do not accept the latest term sheet yet.

The latest proposal has a $36 million maximum outlay, within Brightline’s $40 million authorization, and includes automatic payments to identified members. The fee terms are less favorable to Brightline, but accepting secures a settlement subject to court approval and avoids litigation risk.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement followed arm’s-length negotiations between class counsel and Brightline’s counsel. The parties agreed to a $30 million class fund, with payments to be sent automatically to identified class members without a claims process. The settlement also provides for a fee request of $6 million, subject to court approval; Brightline will not oppose the request, and any amount not awarded will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. The negotiations did not establish that class relief was agreed independently before attorneys’ fees were discussed: the proposals addressed class relief and fees together, and the final agreement followed discussion of both. The Court retains authority to determine whether the requested fees and all other settlement terms are fair, reasonable, and adequate.
